items.readable_text:
Content:
Dividing very large numbers can take some effort. Thankfully, there are some rules that allow us to determine whether one number is divisible by another without having to carry out the division!

Content:
A number is divisible by [MATH: 2] if the last digit is an even number. In other words, if the last digit is [MATH: {\color{blue}{0}},{\color{blue}{2}},{\color{blue}{4}},{\color{blue}{6}},] or [MATH: {\color{blue}{8}},] then the number is divisible by [MATH: 2.]

Content:
For example, the following numbers are divisible by [MATH: 2] because their last digit is even.
[MATH: 51{\color{blue}{0}}, \qquad 785{\color{blue}{2}}, \qquad 232,65{\color{blue}{4}}, \qquad 197,478,24{\color{blue}{6}}, \qquad 578,197,478,24{\color{blue}{8}}]

Content:
On the other hand, the following numbers are not divisible by [MATH: 2] because their last digit is not even.
[MATH: 35{\color{red}{1}}, \qquad 547{\color{red}{3}}, \qquad 58,68{\color{red}{5}}, \qquad 239,63{\color{red}{7}}, \qquad 100,000,000,00{\color{red}{9}}]

Content:
We also have some easy divisibility rules for [MATH: 5] and [MATH: 10.] Again, they depend only on the last digit:

Content:
- A number is divisible by [MATH: 5] if the last digit is [MATH: 5] or [MATH: 0.]
- A number is divisible by [MATH: 10] if the last digit is [MATH: 0.]

Content:
